title: Comparison of strict and enhanced system operation models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes below have $\ell$ invertible and use small pro-etale sites in the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. For each scheme $W$, set $B_{W,n}=(A_n)_W$ and $\widehat R_W=\lim_nB_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the strict semilinear system category $\mathscr S_W$ of $B_{W,n}$-modules with quotient-linear transitions, and its unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $\mathcal R_W$ for simultaneous derived reduction, $U_W$ for exact restriction to $\widehat R_W$-module towers and $\mathcal L_W=R\lim U_W$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus].

Let $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion and $p:Z\to Y$ a morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the ringed sequence sites [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], let $J_j^{\mathrm{str}}$ be exact extension by zero and $S_p^{\mathrm{str}}$ the total right derived functor of levelwise $p_*$, computed by a resolution of the entire system. On the enhanced section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] let $J_j^{\mathrm{sec}},S_p^{\mathrm{sec}}$ be the corresponding operations, and let $\Phi_W$ denote its strictification equivalence. There is a specified natural equivalence on EVERY derived semilinear input $M$,
$$\Phi_Y S_p^{\mathrm{sec}}J_j^{\mathrm{sec}}M\simeq S_p^{\mathrm{str}}J_j^{\mathrm{str}}\Phi_XM.$$
It intertwines the derived adjunction units and counits, the quotient-coefficient direct-image comparisons formed as counit transposes, and arbitrary derived system morphisms, including all composition homotopies. After applying $U_Y$ it is an isomorphism in the derived category of whole towers. It is constructed by comparison of the simultaneous resolutions; it is not an isomorphism chosen from evaluations in the ordinary derived categories.
